claims.text: Stainless steel has a native passivating oxide layer.
The native passivating oxide layer of stainless steel is insufficient under extreme corrosive conditions.
Laser cladding can deposit a refractory high-entropy-alloy coating on a steel surface.
The refractory high-entropy-alloy coating can be deposited specifically on stainless steel.
A data-driven approach can optimize the laser-cladding process parameters for this application.
High chloride concentrations and elevated temperatures are examples of conditions in which the native stainless-steel surface may fail to provide reliable protection.
Optimized laser-cladding parameters generate a refined, uniform dendritic microstructure in the cladding layer.
Optimized laser-cladding parameters enhance metallurgical bonding of the cladding layer.
Optimized laser cladding produces a coating with homogeneous composition and controlled microstructure.
The homogeneous, controlled coating microstructure forms a dense protective barrier.
The coating barrier mitigates localized corrosion under aggressive conditions.
The coating barrier improves overall surface stability under aggressive conditions.
The laser-cladded refractory high-entropy-alloy coating will significantly reduce the corrosion rate relative to unmodified stainless steel.
The coating will extend the durability of stainless steel in aggressive corrosive environments.
Insufficiently optimized laser-cladding parameters may produce poor coating adhesion or non-uniform microstructures.
Poor adhesion or a non-uniform microstructure may compromise the coating's protective effect.
